gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Lectron's own store sells the UL 2252 80A Tesla-to-J1772 adapter for $129.99 today (2026-11-17). That is only $30 more than Lectron's older 48A UL 2251 model ($99.99), $40 below the $169.99 Amazon price, and $20 below the $149.99 ChatGPT showed. It is also $65 less than the uncertified TeslaTap Mini 60A ($194.96), so the certified adapter is cheaper than the TeslaTap Mini.
standout_why: Compared against evandcharger.com (lists Lectron 80A at $169.99, EVDANCE at $49.99 and Leviton, but not TeslaTap or Lectron 48A pricing), thechargecurve.com Lectron-vs-A2Z (Lectron $119.99 on a 48A listing, A2Z with no price, FOCSPROD 60A UL 2252 at $57.99, EVDANCE $49.99), plugandrange.com (Lectron 48A only, $119.99) and ChatGPT's own cards (Lectron 80A $149.99, A2Z $111.42). None has the maker-store price for the Lectron 80A or 48A. None sets the 80A model's small premium over the 48A, or its lower price than TeslaTap, side by side. thisWATT's cited guide could not be opened (SSL certificate error), so it was not compared. FOCSPROD's UL 2252 60A at $57.99 is already on thechargecurve, so the budget-certified finding is only partly new.
decides: Confirms the Lectron 80A UL 2252 as the pick and strengthens it. Bought direct, it costs $129.99. The older 48A model ChatGPT recommended in the second chat saves only $30 and gives up the UL 2252 listing and the temperature sensor. TeslaTap Mini 60A / 80A cost $65 / $95 more with no certification stated. The only certified option that undercuts it is FOCSPROD 60A (UL 2252 in the Amazon title, $57.99), which is a budget alternate rather than the pick. Our page's prices ($149.99 for 80A, $112.99 for 48A) are stale and should become $129.99 and $99.99 at Lectron's store.
